title: One row of game field is hidden in landscape mode.
body:
**Describe the bug**
Game field is too big in landscape mode.

When the device is in landscape mode, the game field is too wide by one row in the progressive and fixed size game modes.

**To Reproduce**
1. Rotate the device into landscape mode.
2. Select new game and "Progressive" or "Fixed size"

Actual behavior: One row on the left is hidden partially under the game ui.
**Expected behavior**
The whole play field fits on the screen.

**Screenshots**
![Wrong game size in landscape](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2601296/138570463-4c44ff8f-5bc7-4bd7-b188-697988b5df52.PNG)

**Android Version:**
11, Pixel 3a.

**App Version**
versionCode 1500021
versionName '15.0.2'

It looks like right now, the calculation for the screen size only uses the system UI size to calculate the height. In landscape mode, it should use those measurements to adjust the width.

Current code in class `MinefieldRepository.baseStandardSize`
```Kotlin
val verticalGap = if (dimensionRepository.navigationBarHeight() > 0)
    VERTICAL_STANDARD_GAP else VERTICAL_STANDARD_GAP_WITHOUT_BOTTOM
...
val calculatedWidth = ((width / fieldSize).toInt() - HORIZONTAL_STANDARD_GAP)
val calculatedHeight = ((height / fieldSize).toInt() - verticalGap)
```

title: [BUG] Bombing with Hotkey while digging deeper bombs the old layer, wasting energy
body:
**Info**
 - OS: [e.g. Windows 10] Ubuntu 20.04
 - Browser [e.g. Chrome, Safari, Firefox] [alexislours] Pokeclicker Client
 - Version [e.g. `v1.0.0`] v1.2.0.deb

**Description:**
<!-- a clear description of the bug -->
The bombing hotkey is not disabled while the game is 'digging deeper' in the underground.  Thus, it is possible to use the hotkey to bomb an already fully cleared layer, wasting mining energy.

**Steps to Reproduce:**
<!-- steps to reproduce the behavior -->
1. Go to Underground
2. Mine a layer completely
3. Click the Bomb hotkey just as the game begins digging deeper
4. Notice that the bomb went off on the cleared layer, as the new layer hasn't been bombed, and some tiles (depending on how cleared the previously cleared layer was) could be seen being removed by the bomb on the old layer.

**Expected Behavior:**
<!-- a clear description of what you expected to happen -->
I'd expect that if the bomb hotkey was used during the 'digging deeper' it would be applied to the new layer, or the hotkey would be disabled like the button is while the digging deeper animation occurs.  

**Screenshots:**
<!-- If applicable, add screenshots to help explain your problem. -->


**Additional Information:**
<!-- add any other info about the problem here -->
The timing on this bug is a bit finnicky, as I have gotten the bomb hotkey to bomb a new layer before you can push the bomb button again, but if you push the bomb hotkey during most of the digging deeper animation, it will bomb the old layer.  It's obviously not a serious issue, as you can just not bomb during that animation, but it is a bug so I figured I'd report it.

title: Theme Hospital finder attempts to access network locations
body:
Win10, 0.65-beta2

On the portable, at first launch (config missing) if you press no to the prompt only the command window will display. About 20 seconds later the application loads -- locks the mouse but doesn't show the window until you Alt-tab.

Edit: TheApp:init() seems to be responsible for that.

Edit2: Something in this loop causes freezing up after the first pass (don't have line numbers at the mo), but it's where we look for game data.

```lua
    for _, dir in pairs(possible_locations) do
      if status then break end
      for _, folder in pairs(possible_folders) do
        local path = dir .. pathsep .. folder

        if lfs.attributes(path, "mode") == "directory" and self:isThemeHospitalPath(path) then
          print("Game data found at: " .. path)
          print("This will be written to the config file")
          self.config.theme_hospital_install = path
          status, _ = self.fs:setRoot(path)
          break
        end
      end
```

Looks like this directory entry (windows tries to connect to network locations with \\\\): ``dir     \\Documents``
i.e. this entry in ``possible_locations``: ``      user_dir and (user_dir .. pathsep ..  "Documents"):``

_Originally posted by @lewri in https://github.com/CorsixTH/CorsixTH/issues/1911#issuecomment-851643600_

title: [Bug]: Scrolling certain packs causes "RageBitmapTexture: Couldn't load <File>: Too many open files"
body:
### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [X] I have searched the existing issues

### Contact Details

You can reply here or get my attention faster on twitter @zhu346p

### Version Info

Latest available release

### What operating system are you seeing the problem on?

macOS

### Bug Behavior

Tested on MacOS both 11.6 and 12.3 (other OS versions untested) with Apple Silicon M1 translated with rosetta2

If a pack contains video assets, scrolling through of them will cause a "Too many open files" prompt to come up and keep recurring. On version 0.71.1 you may crash to the crash handler but I have not gotten this on 0.71.2 yet.

For some reason crashing to the crash handler on MacOS didn't give me a crashlog text file. Despite this happening numerous times in the past few months testing it out my crash folder is empty.




### Expected Behavior

You should be able to scroll normally without encountering error popups, regardless of whether the pack contains videos or not.

### Reproduction Steps

1. Run the game
2. Select a pack that contains songs that have video assets
3. Scroll through the list of songs for about a minute
4. The errors will start popping up

[Refer to this video for the reproduction steps. ](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1UcEvgdYMvI)

Both tests done with the same pack. 
Folder titled "Crash" has all the video assets like a normal download would.
Folder that is titled normally has all video assets (.mp4, .avi) removed and does not crash regardless of how long I scroll the list.

Here are the logs from the runs in the video:

[2022_04_08-10_44_36.log](https://github.com/etternagame/etterna/files/8448172/2022_04_08-10_44_36.log)
[2022_04_08-10_48_38.log](https://github.com/etternagame/etterna/files/8448174/2022_04_08-10_48_38.log)

### Anything else?

I have done a lot of testing over the last few months to determine what causes this. If you delete mp4 files but keep avi files, it still returns the issue. Same happens if you only delete avi files.

In general there seems to be something weird with the handling of video on macOS. Not sure if this is apple silicon specific but the reason this test is done with 'Til Death is because if you try this with Rebirth and the pack thumbnail is a .mp4, the folder icon containing a mp4 thumbnail causes a crash that bypasses the crash handler, and returns you an OS crash dump (segfault). (Obviously a separate issue but still both tests lead me to believe that video files are the issue here)

title: [BUG] crosshair adjustment
body:
**Describe the bug**
There's an issue with the crosshair. Left hooks land much lower than expected, whereas right hooks land much higher than expected. Which as you can imagine, makes it quite annoying to test ODMG logic. Issue did not occur before https://github.com/AoTTG-2/AoTTG-2/commit/083f550fd58b0cf09d7c253301ff472776d05f5b, and was caused somewhere during the Pull Requests

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Aim at something with your hooks
2. Left hook will hit below the crosshair whereas the right hook will hit above the crosshair

**Expected behavior**
It's expected that the hook will land exactly where the crosshair aimed it at
